title: feat(objectql,driver-sql): PostgreSQL buckets a non-UTC reference timezone in the database (ADR-0053 D2 as amended)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9Ux14k8AfX9D3xKvZZ1Vr7j)_
Fixes #33697

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches driver capability bits or where a zoned date bucket runs; the bit is read by the engine, and an app author writes the same `timezone` as before.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：PostgreSQL 上按非 UTC 时区(如 Asia/Taipei、Europe/Berlin)的日/周/月/季/年分组，改为在数据库里用 `AT TIME ZONE` 分桶，不再把整批行拉进应用内存;SQLite、MySQL 等其余驱动照旧走内存分桶。
- 为什么改：执行维护者裁决「PG 在库里算，修订 ADR」(ADR-0053 D2 修订已合);多数用户不在 UTC,他们的每个日报/月报此前都走慢路径。
- 风险与回滚：只改分桶表达式，权限范围与租户墙仍在同一条 WHERE;库内结果与内存结果逐桶对等(PG 16 实测，含柏林两次夏令时切换);回滚即撤本 PR,引擎自动回到内存路径。
- 先看:`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts`(时区只绑定一次、GROUP BY 按序号)、`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`(按运行时解析后的时区名分派)、`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts`(新契约类型)。
- 两分钟验证：起一个 PG(服务器时区 Asia/Shanghai),`OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=… pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run src/sql-driver-33697-zoned-date-bucket.test.ts`,预期 61 过 1 跳过(MySQL 未配)。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

ADR-0053 Phase 2 D2, as amended for this card (PR #33774), executed:

- **`@objectstack/spec`**: a new live driver capability bit, `supports.zonedDateBucketing` (`DriverCapabilitiesSchema`, with its reader in the same change, per the schema docblock's bar for a new bit), and a new contract type `DriverAggregateQuery` = `DriverQuery` plus `timezone`, which `IDataDriver.aggregate` now receives. Kept off `DriverQuery` on purpose: `find()` / `count()` take that type and would silently drop a zone. Review item (c): the `IDataDriver.aggregate` jsdoc ("a driver never sees" a non-UTC zone) and the `timezone` jsdoc in `data-engine.zod.ts` are rewritten; `DriverOptions.timezone` (the execution-context zone, read for autonumber) is left untouched as the carrier it is.
- **`@objectstack/objectql`**: `engine.aggregate` judges the request's `timezone` through the runtime (`judgeBucketZone`: the `resolvedOptions().timeZone` of an `Intl.DateTimeFormat`). Resolves to `UTC` (`Etc/UTC`, `GMT`, `Zulu`) → the native UTC path (review item d). Resolves to an area/location name → pushed down AS the resolved name (`CST` → `America/Chicago`, `US/Eastern` → `America/New_York`, `Etc/GMT+5` as itself) when the driver declares the bit and has `aggregate()`. Anything else (`EST5EDT`, `+08:00`, an unresolvable string), or a driver without the bit → the in-memory path, unchanged (review item e). The raw string never reaches a driver. The relation-group-join statement gets the zone the same way.
- **`@objectstack/driver-sql`**: declares the bit on PostgreSQL only (`zonedDateBucketing: this.isPostgres`; `TursoDriver` is SQLite and inherits `false`). `buildDateBucketExpr` takes the zone: `to_char((col)::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE ?, fmt)` with the zone bound; a `Field.date` keeps its calendar-day arm under every zone; every other dialect answers `null` for a zone. Review item (a): the zoned bucket is stated once, in the select list, and the GROUP BY names its select-list position — spelled twice, PostgreSQL numbers the two `?` as `$1` / `$2` and refuses with 42803 (measured, ablation A1 below). A direct `aggregate()` call carrying a zone is judged before anything compiles: a dialect without the bit refuses `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`/501, and a zone string that is not its own resolved area/location name refuses `INVALID_QUERY`/400 — never read as UTC. `dateBucketSql` takes the zone too, for the echo.
- **`@objectstack/service-analytics`** (review item c, the dry run and `dateBucketSql`): `ObjectQLStrategy.generateSql` reads the zone the way the engine does (`echoBucketZone`) and asks the `dateBucketSql` hook with the resolved zone; PostgreSQL answers the zoned expression the database groups by and the dry run prints it (and it runs); every driver that buckets the zone in memory answers nothing and the dry run refuses as before. The plugin bridge, `DatasetScopedStrategyContext.dateBucketSql` and `AnalyticsServiceConfig.dateBucketSql` gain the optional `timezone` argument.

Review item (b), SQLite: it does not declare the bit, so every non-UTC zone stays in memory there. The amendment allows a fixed-offset zone to be bucketed in SQL; this PR does not take that option (see Acceptance notes).

## Tests

- New `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-33697-zoned-date-bucket.test.ts` (dialect matrix): on live PostgreSQL, every bucket `aggregate()` answers equals the in-memory label (`bucketDateKey`, `@objectstack/core`; `Field.date` with no zone, as `bucketCalendarDay` does) for Europe/Berlin across both 2026 DST changes, Asia/Taipei, America/New_York (west of UTC, the `Field.date` axis), America/Chicago and Etc/GMT+5, at all five granularities, on both column types; the bucket after a plain key, aliased, under a `where` with bindings; refusals with `code` + `status` for `CST`, `US/Eastern`, `+08:00`, `EST5EDT`, `Bogus/Zone`. On SQLite (and MySQL where provisioned): no bit, 501 refusal, UTC and a no-bucket query served. A fixture-sensitivity pin keeps the parity non-vacuous.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-timezone.test.ts`: a new describe pins the dispatch spelling by spelling (resolved names sent; UTC aliases native with no zone; `EST5EDT` / `+08:00` / `Bogus/Zone` in memory; no bit or `false` in memory; no zone for a query without a date bucket).
- Tests changed because the behaviour they pinned changed by the ruling, each named:
  - `packages/spec/src/data/driver.test.ts` — the audited capability shape is 6 live bits + 31 tombstones (was 5); absence and a non-boolean value pinned for the new bit.
  - `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/objectql-echo-date-bucket.test.ts` — the live PostgreSQL cell now pins the zoned pushdown (the driver groups once, the rows equal the zone's calendar, the dry run prints the zoned expression and it runs) instead of the refusal; SQLite keeps the refusal; the per-dialect block's hook passes the zone, PostgreSQL prints the zoned expression, and new cases pin `+08:00` / `EST5EDT` refusing and `Etc/UTC` / `GMT` printing the UTC expression.
  - `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/objectql-echo-bucket-enumeration.test.ts` — `Etc/UTC` moves to the UTC class and `GMT` joins it (it was pinned in the in-memory class because the engine compared the raw string); the "any other zone" class becomes "an area/location zone" (pushed down on a driver declaring the bit, asserted per face) plus a new "no area/location name" class; the driver surface takes the zone argument.

## Acceptance notes

- SQLite fixed-offset pushdown (the amendment's optional arm) is not taken: deciding "fixed-offset over the instants being bucketed" needs the column's min/max before the statement (Asia/Taipei has pre-1980 transitions), and Etc/GMT±N is the only zone fixed over all history. Every SQLite zone stays in the in-memory path, which the amendment keeps correct. A follow-up card can measure it. Disposition: dropped — no measured pull for SQLite zoned dashboards, and the only zones fixed over all history are Etc/GMT±N; the in-memory path stays correct (area o2-F, under the startup no-expansion axis).
- The engine (`judgeBucketZone`), the driver (`resolvedAreaZone`) and the analytics echo (`echoBucketZone`) each state the same resolution rule; `@objectstack/core` is the natural shared home, outside this card's file surface. The analytics enumeration pin holds the engine and the echo together; the driver's copy only refuses. Disposition: filed #34544 (one shared resolution rule; Blocked-by #33697).
- The tz data in PostgreSQL and in Node's ICU are two copies (the residual the amendment records); the parity pins run where both agree on the fixture zones.

## Verification

All local, on PostgreSQL 16.15 with the server at `Asia/Shanghai` and the process at `TZ=America/New_York`.

<details><summary>Packages: test + typecheck</summary>

- `@objectstack/driver-sql` test (with the live PostgreSQL cell): 267 files passed, 4 skipped; 5513 tests passed, 128 skipped (MySQL / SQL Server cells unprovisioned). typecheck exit 0.
- `@objectstack/objectql` test: green; typecheck exit 0. `engine-aggregate-timezone.test.ts` 17/17.
- `@objectstack/service-analytics` test (live PostgreSQL cell included): 218 files, 5835 passed, 34 skipped. typecheck exit 0.
- `@objectstack/driver-turso` test: 100 files passed, 1 skipped; typecheck exit 0.
- `@objectstack/spec` test: the two red cases before the pin update were the audited capability shape (`driver.test.ts`), now 60/60; typecheck exit 0. `check:generated --fix` regenerated `api-surface/contracts.json`, `export-origins/contracts.json` and the three `content/docs/references/data/driver*.mdx` pages.
- New zoned-bucket matrix: 61 passed, 1 skipped (live MySQL).
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (each restored, `git diff HEAD` empty after all four)</summary>

- A1 driver, review item (a): the GROUP BY spells the zoned bucket again (`groupByRaw(bucket.sql, bucket.bindings)`) → 26 failed / 35 passed; PostgreSQL answers 42803 "must appear in the GROUP BY clause".
- A2 driver: the zone binding replaced by `'UTC'` → 16 failed / 45 passed (every `Field.datetime` zone cell whose labels differ from UTC; the `Field.date` cells stay green, as they must).
- A3 engine: the capability bit not read → 5 failed / 12 passed (every pushdown case).
- A4 engine, review item (d): the resolved-`UTC` arm deleted → 3 failed / 14 passed (`Etc/UTC`, `GMT`, `Zulu`).
</details>

<details><summary>Derived gates</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` on head `03414032`: 128 commands, each run with stdin from /dev/null, all exit 0; `--ran` reconciliation: 128 derived, 128 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
</details>
